 SALT LAKE CITY (KUTV) — Two dresser recalls are raising concerns about tip-over and entrapment hazards that could seriously injure or kill children, according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission.
 The CPSC says both dressers can be unstable if they are not anchored to a wall. The agency says no injuries have been reported in either recall.
 The SOOWERY 8-Drawer Fabric Dresser was sold online at Amazon.com from December 2025 through August 2026 for about $106. Consumers should stop using the dresser if it is not anchored to the wall, keep it in an area children cannot access and contact SOOWERY for a full refund.

 The Jocoevol 6-Drawer Dresser was sold online at Amazon.com from December 2024 through July 2026 for about $160. Consumers should stop using it if it is not anchored to the wall, keep it in an area children cannot access and contact Yinklev for a full refund.
 The CPSC says consumers will be asked to mark the recalled dressers and send photos to the companies before disposing of them. 
 For SOOWERY dresser refund instructions, contact SOOWERYrecall@outlook.com. For Jocoevol dresser instructions, contact Jocoevoldresserrecall@outlook.com.
